conventions.how_to_read: Every entry has either `command` (round-1 probes: the exact argv + prompt that was typed) or `harness` + `commands` (probes run by the committed scripts in harness/, relative to fixtures/muse-code: `commands` is the script's own log of every action it executed, in order: `set -m`, background launches with their redirections, readiness loops, watchdogs, signals as delivered, `wait ...; echo $? > ...rc`, child-process checks). No entry abbreviates a command or prompt with `...`. Entries with `round1_raw` were captured before the harness existed, by typing the command inline; the command shown is the exact argv + prompt.
conventions.placeholders: <WORKSPACE> = the git worktree muse ran in (a linked worktree under $HOME unless the entry says workspace_root=tmp, which is a plain directory under /tmp used by early round-1 probes); <PROBE_HOME> = a directory under $HOME that is a sibling of the workspace (target of the outside-workspace write probes; for the round-1 probes it is literally $HOME/muse-spike-probe); <SPIKE_DIR> = the harness scratch root under $HOME; <CFG>/<DATA> = per-run XDG_CONFIG_HOME / XDG_DATA_HOME (mode 0700; muse/auth.json inside <CFG> is a symlink to the operator's auth.json, never read or committed); <HOME> = the operator's home; <SPIKE_TMP> = round-1 scratch under /tmp; <DECK_ID>/<WORKTREE> = redacted Agent Deck deck id and worktree path inside settings; <id-N>/<call-N>/<resp-N> = stable per-fixture stand-ins for uuids / call ids / response ids (shared by the command, stderr and events of one entry); <ts> = recorded_at. Process ids in harness commands are the real pids of that run.
conventions.sanitization: Applied to parsed JSON string VALUES only: field names such as call_id are never rewritten. Agent Deck MCP tool-result bodies are replaced by `<redacted MCP payload: N bytes>`. String values longer than 400 chars are cut with a `…[truncated N chars]` marker.
conventions.compaction: Committed captures keep only: run.terminal.completed|failed, tool.result, task.lifecycle.failed, tool-level task.lifecycle.side_effect_intent (operation `tool:*`), the first run.model.configured, task.lifecycle.status events carrying error_kind rate_limited, runtime.session (session-log excerpt), and run.output.delta only when the run never reached a terminal event. 01-exec-success keeps every event as a full-envelope example. `sequence` numbers therefore have gaps. `stdout_lines_raw`, `stdout_lines_committed` and `dropped_by_type` are computed by harness/build-fixtures.py from the raw capture and re-verified against the files by muse-code-fixtures.test.ts.
conventions.settings: `settings_profile` names an entry of `settings_profiles` = the exact contents of <CFG>/muse/settings.json for that run (null = no settings file).
conventions.exact: true = command + prompt + settings reproduce the run; false entries say why in exact_reason.
